expectations.evidence: Three clearly labeled problem areas (Redundancy, No-op instructions, Verbose phrasing) plus an optimized prompt. Exactly 3 recommendations — within the 3–5 range.

expectations.text: At least one recommendation explains WHY the change saves tokens (not just what to change)
expectations.evidence: 'The model doesn't skip reading' — explains why the 'read thoroughly' instruction is a no-op. 'These are instructional habits from human writing that don't translate to LLM prompting.'

expectations.text: Response includes a token savings estimate (percentage or count)
expectations.evidence: '~47 tokens, ~64% reduction' and 'cuts ~83 tokens (~64%) while preserving all functional constraints.'

expectations.text: Response opens with a one-sentence diagnosis of the prompt's main inefficiency
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'Analysis of the original prompt (~130 tokens):' — a label/header. The actual diagnosis ('The prompt has three main problems:') follows but is not a single synthesized diagnosis sentence.

expectations.text: Response acknowledges or highlights the high-volume context (cost impact at scale)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly recommends prompt caching 'regardless of how many times it's reused' and frames it as 'the highest-ROI optimization for high-volume pipelines.' Addresses scale directly.

eval_feedback.overall: Good discrimination. The diagnosis assertion catches a real structural difference — the baseline jumps to analysis without a framing statement, while the skill consistently opens with a clear single-sentence diagnosis.
